x: Du'aine Ladejo went out hard, as did the Welshman Iwan Thomas but Roger Black was in the form of his life and coming strongly off the bend he came through for a British Record 44.39 while Ladejo had to be content with 2nd in a personal (and Club) best of 44.66.

Iwan Thomas was a close third just ahead of Andrew Walcott who was showing a late season return to form. In the 10000m Jim Estall, fresh from holiday and claiming to be unfit, had a good tussle with former record holder Julian Goater and moved our point score along nicely.

A 45.5 clocking made him second fastest of the quartet but with top men Iwan Thomas and Mark Richardson taking a breather before the final, no-one had any complaints about the final selection on this occasion.

On the start line Sean Baldock faced no less an adversary than Iwan Thomas seeking proof of a return to fitness prior to next week's AAA's. And it was Sean hitting the lead at 200 who held on well for a stunning victory in a sub 46 timing which was his fastest since the Sydney Olympics.
Dominic later achieved star status by running the last leg of the long relay in an official split time of 47.4 as he chased Iwan Thomas (Newham) and Chris Rawlinson (Trafford).

The current British record stands at 44.36 secs, set by fellow Welshman Iwan Thomas in July 1997, and while Benjamin does not believe he will have to record that time to make the final, he admits he may have to do so in order to win a medal.

Judging by that I can run 0.25secs quicker,” which would put him within sight of fellow Welshman Iwan Thomas’ British record. Benjamin feels he can match the European gold medal Thomas won seven years ago when Gothenburg hosts the championship next season.

After placing 5th at the World Championships, Tim has just lowered our club 400-metre record to 44:56 in Monaco, to put him within a couple of tenths of Iwan Thomas’s British record, which Roger Black feels Tim will one day smash.
